items.title: Liverpool and the Slave Trade: Profits of Human Bondage
items.author: History Is Now Magazine
items.description: In the early 18th century, Liverpool entered the transatlantic slave trade, the darkest chapter in its history. The remnants of this period can still be seen today, scattered throughout the city centre and beyond. From the waterfront to the Town Hall, reminders of Liverpool’s involvement remain embedded in its landscape. This raises the question: what did the slave trade actually mean for the people of Liverpool, and how did an economy built around Atlantic commerce transform the city's workpla…

items.author: Sara Beth Haring
items.description: by Charles Finch For fans of historical mystery, a perfectly poured cup of tea or a soothing nighttime tonic often signals impending doom. items.title: The Football War: The Hundred-Hour War between El Salvador and Honduras
items.author: History Is Now Magazine
items.description: The very title, “Football War,” is misleading. This is not a story about rivalry between football clubs and their fans. It was a brief conflict fought between El Salvador and Honduras in July 1969, and it was only tangentially connected to the sport itself. The name comes from its timing: the fighting broke out just weeks after the two countries had played a bitterly contested series of qualifying matches for the 1970 World Cup. items.author: History Is Now Magazine
items.description: The Avignon Papacy (1309-1376) was the period during which seven successive popes resided at Avignon, in modern-day southern France, rather than at Rome. items.author: History Is Now Magazine
items.description: As one of the wealthiest figures in American history, Andrew Carnegie left behind a legacy that remains deeply contested among historians and the public alike. While his name is permanently memorialized on thousands of public libraries, universities, and cultural institutions across the globe, his rise to unprecedented economic dominance was achieved through methods that raise fundamental questions regarding the true human cost of his late-in-life generosity.
